submitted.rationale: Highest measured EQE was 0.00903% at 2.1 eV, at index 3 (Pb 0.74). XRD shows a stable Pb2Sb2O7 pyrochlore across the library, plus PbO at the Pb-rich end. The PbO SCAN gap is 1.50 eV, making it the likely 2.1 eV absorber. EQE rose from about 6e-5% at the Sb-rich end (index 24) to 0.0081% at index 0 (Pb 0.83) and 0.0090% at index 3. That suggests a mixed PbO + pyrochlore region performs best.

rejected.reason: Measured 0.0081%, slightly below index 3. It is dominated by PbO with less pyrochlore.
Measured 6.1e-5%. It is nearly phase-pure pyrochlore with an HSE gap of about 2.5 eV, so it absorbs little at 2.1 eV.

consultations.verdict: Pyrochlore Pb2Sb2O7 is stable (hull 0) with HSE gap ~2.5 eV, above the 2.1 eV photon energy. Index 0 also contains PbO (XRD match 0.81); MEGNet puts its gap at 3.36 eV, but PbO polymorphs have experimental gaps as low as ~1.9 eV. Sub-gap absorption at 2.1 eV is therefore most plausible at the Pb-rich end. Weak support for measuring index 0.

The SCAN-fidelity gap for the Pb2Sb2O7 pyrochlore is 1.94 eV (HSE gave 2.5). The pyrochlore may therefore be near or below the 2.1 eV photon energy. Index 24 is nearly phase-pure pyrochlore with no PbO peak at Q 2.037. Index 0 (PbO-rich) gave a low EQE, so moderate support for probing the Sb-rich pyrochlore end.

The SCAN gap for PbO is 1.50 eV, below 2.1 eV, so the PbO phase is the likely 2.1 eV absorber. That agrees with the measured EQE: 0.0081% at Pb-rich index 0 versus 0.00006% at Sb-rich index 24. Index 3 (Pb 0.74) should still contain PbO, mixed with more pyrochlore, which could form a beneficial heterojunction. The GP UCB also picks index 3. Support.
